headline: What to Watch Out For When Budgeting for a Home Addition
articleBody: Budgeting for a home addition can be tricky, and it's easy to make a few common mistakes that can inflate costs. One of the biggest pitfalls is having an unrealistic budget from the get-go. Construction can always have unexpected twists, so it's wise to build in a buffer—think 10-15% of your total project cost—for unforeseen expenses. Another mistake is ignoring permits and building codes. These aren't just bureaucratic hurdles; they ensure safety and structural integrity, and cutting corners here can lead to costly rework or fines. Poor structural planning, especially concerning the foundation, is another major misstep. You also need to consider how the addition will integrate with existing plumbing, electrical, and HVAC systems. Failing to account for these connections can lead to significant extra costs and functionality issues down the line. To avoid these issues, work with a contractor who provides a clear, written scope and manages change orders transparently.
